reports.text:
Fish ’N Stuff (501-834-5733) said crappie are still behind the jetties and in cuts in the jettings. reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Cane Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Shelley Burr at Cane Creek State Park, (870-628-4714) said one angler last Thursday was buying crickets to fish for crappie from a boat in the lake; no report on how his catches went. Three customers also bought crickets earlier in the week for some crappie fishing on the bank. This week, one crappie angler Monday was targeting the fish with minnows. Another angler on Tuesday reported that he had no luck crappie fishing.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Charles fishing report
reports.text:
Shelly Jeffrey at Lake Charles State Park (870-878-6595) said crappie, bass and bream are all biting at the lake. Bream and crappie are beginning to bite shallow. Crappie are good on jigs, minnows and worms. Black bass are good, but Shelly was unable to get baits used from the anglers.
Terry Morris caught a 2-pound, 9-ounce white crappie on a jig minnow at the Overlook boat ramp on March 14, she reported.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ouachita fishing report
reports.text:
Todd Gadberry at Mountain Harbor Resort and Spa (870-867-2191/800-832-2276 out-of-state) reports that black bass are excellent. Crappie are very good and relating to brush in the 8- to 20-foot range.
Darryl Morris of Family Fishing Trips (501-844-5418) has been doing his fishing at lakes Ouachita and DeGray in recent days and said for both, “ Springtime transition for the crappie is on. reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: White River/Arkansas River fishing report
reports.text: In shallow reservoirs and lakes, the crappie are biting very well. Bass tournaments in southeastern Arkansas are kicking off — they are catching good numbers in these events.

reports.text:
Crappie guide Eric Watts of Natural State Fishing (501-548-8990) said, “ We had a phenomenal week of fishing last week through the weekend!
“That said, I’ll be exploring some of our other awesome crappie fishing locations across Central Arkansas over the next few weeks.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Arkansas River fishing report
reports.text: The University of Arkansas at Pine Bluff Bass Fishing Team had no new reports with cold conditions through much of February and part of March.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Arkansas River (Little Rock Area Pools) fishing report
reports.text: The bass can be found in 3-6 feet of water in any live grass/green grass areas on the bank.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Beaver Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Crappie are starting to move shallow 10 feet or less.
Bass are in all prespawn areas and will continue to move up.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Bull Shoals Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Bass fishing has been a little slower than average.
(updated 3-13-2025) Crappie 101 Guide Service (870-577-2045) says crappie are in the creeks — just smaller pods and the jig bite has been decent.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Cane Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Shelley Burr at Cane Creek State Park, (870-628-4714) said they had an angler late in February who bought minnows to go out on his boat on the lake and caught a few crappie.
Shelley reports that a man came in last weekend bragging about catching 60 or more crappie using minnows — he caught a bronze-colored crappie that weighed 2 pounds. Another customer was attempting crappie fishing from the shoreline with minnows that weekend as it warmed some, while another customer bought some crappie bait at the store to fish out of his boat for crappie on Monday the first full week of March. On Sunday, two young gentlemen came into VIC to purchase minnows to crappie fish from spillway side of lake…

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Greers Ferry Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Fish ’N Stuff (501-834-5733) in Sherwood said Greers Ferry Bass fishing has been “hit or miss,” with catching coming as water as deep as 3 feet out to 30 feet, depending on the day.
Crappie are being caught in about 10 feet of water on brushpiles mainly by throwing an eighth-ounce jighead with a Tennessee Shad or Monkey Milk-colored jig.
Crappie should be super shallow out to 30 feet.
You will start running into small groups of five to eight black bass up shallow.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Catherine Tailwater (Below Carpenter Dam) fishing report
reports.text: Crappie will begin migrating toward the dam at the end of this month and should be in full spawning mode by early April.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Charles fishing report
reports.text:
The crappie bite fell off.
However, black bass were good. They are shallow and are talking to redworms for anglers fishing off the shore. Also, bream are good. They also have come up shallow and will bite redworms and jigs near the shoreline.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Maumelle fishing report
reports.text:
Crappie guide Eric Watts of Natural State Fishing (501-548-8990) said the water level is extremely low now, approximately 9 feet below normal pool.
Crappie fishing has been phenomenal! Now is a great time to try your favorite color Original Baby Shad from Bobby Garland Crappie Baits.
Before all the deep freeze of last week, though, largemouth bass had been biting well 2-5 feet with others being found deeper and scattered around brush anywhere from 10-20 feet. Spotted bass were good, scattered on drop-offs at 10-20 feet and biting on jerkbaits and jigs. Crappie were good in 20-30 feet in the channel on jigs.

reports.text:

reports.text:
Millwood gave up a couple more fat female donkey, prespawn, largemouth bass full of roe this past week in another high school bass tournament. Levi Whitman, high school freshman, and his partner, Seth Nugent, both from Benton (Louisiana) High School, weighed in a 10.56-pound giant of a largemouth and took Big Bass and top stringer weight in the tournament. There were several guys at the weigh-in talking about another largemouth over 10 pounds caught the same day and released because the other bass anglers who caught it were not in the tournament in the same weekend.”
This comes on the heels of the 13.45-pound largemouth caught in a high school tournament on March 2.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Bull Shoals Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Bass fishing has been a little frustrating with good days followed by pulling your hair out.
(updated 3-20-2025) Crappie 101 Guide Service (870-577-2045) says to look for crappie in the creeks around brushpiles close to 20-ish feet that are found closer to baitfish.

reports.text: Darryl Morris of Family Fishing Trips (501-844-5418) has been doing his fishing at lakes Ouachita and DeGray in recent days and said for both, “ Springtime transition for the crappie is on. reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Blue Mountain Lake fishing report
reports.text: Sheila at Carter Cove Bait-N-More (479-272-4025) says bait customers who stop in there before heading to Blue Mountain Lake say the fishing at Blue Mountain is going well for crappie. “Almost everyone I talk to is saying, ‘Crappie, crappie, crappie’ … Some customers are wanting to catch bream and are requesting crickets, though it’s not time for the bream to be spawning yet.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nimrod fishing report
reports.text:
Fishing for both bass and crappie are good for some, not as good for others.
Black bass are biting spinnerbaits. They’re not large-size bass now. Crappie might come in large, she says, or some small; some with a limit, and some anglers with 2.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Arkansas River (Little Rock Area Pools) fishing report
reports.text: When they water does come down closer to 50,000 cfs and safer for small craft, the cooler water temperature should still allow for some good bass fishing.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Beaver Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are also everywhere, from suspended at 13 feet in 30 feet of water and also on structure in 8-30 feet.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Brewer Lake fishing report
reports.text:
We need some warmer nights to bring up the lake water temperature, and crappie should start biting soon.
Brewer Lake has a new regulation for 2025: The 13- to 16-inch black bass slot limit on Brewer (as well as Lake Barnett in White County) has been replace; now, anglers may keep up to 10 largemouth bass, but only one of those may exceed 16 inches.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Bull Shoals Lake fishing report
reports.text: (updated 3-6-2025) Crappie 101 Guide Service (870-577-2045) says crappie are in the creeks not too far from the shad.

Crappie should be super shallow out to 30 feet.
You will start running into small groups of five to eight black bass up shallow.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Chicot fishing report
reports.text: Crappie reports have been good from AGFC staffers in recent weeks. Anglers putting in from the Connerly Bayou Access have been seeing good results. Lake Chicot, part of Lake Chicot State Park, is home to bluegill, channel catfish, largemouth bass, hybrid striped bass, redear sunfish and other bream, in addition to crappie. If you fish Lake Chicot, Connerly Bayou downstream of Connerly Dam, or Ditch Bayou from Lake Chicot downstream to Ditch Bayou Dam, be aware that crappie shorter than 10 inches must be immediately released and that the crappie daily limit is 20.

reports.text:
Todd Gadberry at Mountain Harbor Resort and Spa (870-867-2191/800-832-2276 out-of-state) reports that black bass are very good.
Crappie are very good and biting over the tops of brush in the 20- to 30-foot range.
The Trader Bill’s Team Trail event was held last weekend on Ouachita, and an 8.99-pounder and 7.74-pound largemouth were among the catches. Marvin Lewis and Phil Lancaster caught a 5-bass stringer of 20.52 pounds, including the Big Bass (8.99 pounds).
Darryl Morris of Family Fishing Trips (501-844-5418) said he has been fishing both lakes Ouachita and Hamilton, and says, “Crappie season is upon us. (Wednesday) I caught crappie as deep as 24 feet when the morning water temperature…

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Millwood Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Mike Siefert at Millwood Lake Guide Service said Wednesday that Millwood Lake gave up a couple more “Millwood Donkeys” this past weekend in a high school bass tournament. Griffin Ralph from Lakeside High School in Hot Springs weighed in a 13.43-pound giant of a largemouth. There was talk at the ramp of another lucky angler with a largemouth over 11 pounds the same weekend. Congratulations to Griffin, that bass is only a few gizzard shad away from a new Millwood Lake record of 14.5 pounds.
* Largemouth bass continue slowing improving over the past two weeks with the warmer conditions, depending on location, but it can been random on high barometric days. Male bass continue cruising shallow…

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Peckerwood Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie, she added, are still “all over the place with this crazy weather.” Use minnows or jigs for crappie. She hasn’t heard anything on the bass so far.

reports.text:
We need some warmer nights to bring up the lake water temperature, and crappie should start biting soon.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Overcup fishing report
reports.text: Bream haven’t started yet but bass and catfish are being caught on yo-yos and jugs using minnows. Crappie are doing well on minnows using rod and reel, as well as on jugs and yo-yos.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Little Maumelle River fishing report
reports.text: Last weekend, black bass were biting from 6 feet all the way up to 3 feet. Anglers nearby were catching crappie in 3-4 feet depth.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Harris Brake Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Harris Brake Lake Resort (501-889-2745) says bass and catfish have been biting well this week. One angler in particular was kayak fishing and caught several largemouth and spotted bass.
Crappie are slow.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Arkansas River (Little Rock Area Pools) fishing report
reports.text:
Fish ’N Stuff (501-834-5733) said bass are active and biting in the backwaters on a three-quarter-ounce white spinnerbait and a half-ounce Brazalo Custom Lures spinnerbait, also in white.
With the river flow up Thursday morning (70,000 cfs), crappie are also mainly in the backwaters and anglers are urged to also stick around those areas because of that higher flow. Fish for crappie around stumps or rock piles and use a blue and chartreuse one-sixteenth-ounce crappie jig. Another way to fish the crappie is to tie on a mini Keitech Swimbait and swimming those around the stumps and grass.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Beaver Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are scattered with the rise but should commit to the banks with this warm weather coming next week.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Bull Shoals Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Black bass are in prespawn. Overall, bass fishing has been fair; it definitely slowed down after the big storm, then the cold front.
If it’s flat and sunny, use a Jewel Peewee Jig in green pumpkin with either a Bass Whacker or Touchdown in orange or blue.
(updated 3-28-2024) Crappie 101 Guide Service reports that crappie are still actively feeding in creeks but the bite has slowed. Crappie are beginning to stage in areas close to spawning grounds.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Cane Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Keyunna Austin at Cane Creek State Park said anglers were fishing for crappie and catfish on Tuesdays and catching both with minnows and liver. Another group was having success catching crappie using redworms.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Craig D. Campbell Lake Conway Reservoir fishing report
reports.text:
Bates Field and Stream (501-470-1846) said the bass “are really doing it right now. The bass are on fire.”
Crappie are “still doing all right” but it’s the bass bite that is really going great.
Crappie are liking jigs about the same as minnows, but it’s especially a minnow bite with the crappie in the evenings.
The pond is more than 60 acres and has bass, crappie, bream and some winter-stocked rainbow trout.
reports.lake: Craig D. Campbell Lake Conway Reservoir

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Greers Ferry Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Some crappie are roaming around chewing while other crappie are roaming and chewing in pole timber or in brush piles — in all places they are suspended 4 feet down to 40 feet.
Black bass are good super shallow out to 50 feet in guts, main lake points or secondary points and biting on Alabama rig, Carolina rig, jerkbaits, football heads or crankbaits and Texas-rigged lizards. Stay around the shad and or spawning areas. Some are now eating topwater baits as well.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Catherine Tailwater (Below Carpenter Dam) fishing report
reports.text:
April also promises the beginning of the crappie spawn, which will add another quality game fish for the public to target.
The rising water does not affect the walleye and crappie bite to the same degree.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ouachita fishing report
reports.text: Todd Gadberry at Mountain Harbor Resort and Spa (870-867-2191/800-832-2276 out-of-state) said black bass are very good.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Millwood Lake fishing report
reports.text:
* Largemouth bass drastically improved activity over the past two weeks. Bass Assassin 5-inch Shads, plastic lizards, Brush Hogs, tubes and spinnerbaits will draw a reaction in 2-6 feet depths. Bill Lewis Crankbaits like the MR-6, the Echo 1.75, and SB-57 MDJ crankbaits were all getting random reaction bites over the past couple of weeks from these active roaming bass in the deeper sections of creek channels or drops from the flats into 8-12 feet structure with stumps present. We caught good numbers of males and females from 3-6 pounds each over the past two weeks on Bass Assassin Shads, lizards and spinnerbaits in the shallow lily pads, grass and buckbrush.
The largemouths’ reaction bites…

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Norfork Lake fishing report
reports.text:
The bass and crappie will move shallow staging for spawn but have not done so yet. The water in the creeks is clearing and good bass fishing is on its way.
Keri landed two nice striped bass and a really good largemouth bass.
Joe was back at finding and catching some really nice walleye, crappie and one striped bass.
Crappie are staging for their spawn, which should happen before long. There are quite a few big slab crappie on or near brush piles back in creeks. The bass are still a little way off for their spawn, but with the early warm weather it might be sooner than normal.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Poinsett fishing report
reports.text:
Anglers have been requesting blue/white as well as pink jigs for crappie as of late, though some anglers reported having success with orange jig skirts. At the bait shop at the park, minnows continue to be the top-selling bait for crappie, though. They are having success in open water from boats as well as from the bank with crappie.
Bass reports have not been as numerous, however. Both bass and crappie are still catch-and-release, whereas with bream and catfish you can keep state limits.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Horseshoe Lake fishing report
reports.text:
The prespawn bite for crappie continues and the fish are extremely scattered.
Male bass are showing up in the shallows.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Arkansas River (Little Rock Area Pools) fishing report
reports.text:
Fish ’N Stuff (501-834-5733) said bass fishing has been getting pretty good out in the Little Rock pool; it’s definitely picking up. Also a white and black buzzbait has been picking up some bass. They are catching bass in the backwaters or in the areas leading into the backwaters, shallow up against any cover whether it be grass, wood or rock.
Crappie also are beginning well now. A black and chartreuse or blue and chartreuse crappie jig will be a good choice, they said.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Beaver Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing should also uptick each day that we get closer to the spawn. Crappie are schooling up on shallow brush waiting to make that last push to the shoreline.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Bull Shoals Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Bass are in early prespawn. Overall, bass fishing has been fair; it definitely slowed down after the big storm, then the cold front.
(updated 3-21-2024) Crappie 101 Guide Service reports that crappie are actively feeding in creeks at times and they are also still finding some on brush piles.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Craig D. Campbell Lake Conway Reservoir fishing report
reports.text:
Minnows and all colors of jigs have been working for crappie up until the last few days. Cranks are good black bass.
The pond is more than 60 acres and has bass, crappie, bream and stocked rainbow trout.
reports.lake: Craig D. Campbell Lake Conway Reservoir

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: DeGray Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Male buck bass were noted swimming through the shallow water. In a bass tournament over the weekend, the biggest bass caught topped 9 pounds, and then it fell off to the 6 pound range from there.
You’re going to want to fish weedless in the shallow areas as bass begin to hit those spots in their run-up to spawning.
The crappie are definitely moving up shallower and in transition to spawn.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Greers Ferry Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Crappie are either roaming around chewing while others are doing the same in pole timber or in brush piles. Black bass are good super shallow out to 50 feet in guts, main lake points or secondary points, and biting on an Alabama rig, C-rig, jerkbaits, football heads or crankbaits.
The bass fishing has been really good overall, and anglers are using a lot of different things.
The crappie have been doing “pretty well,” they add.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Horseshoe Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Crappie are Scattered.
“Look for the crappie to continue to be scattered until we have a stable weather pattern at which point they should make their move to the shallows.
“In talking with several anglers (Wednesday) found that there were a few bass being caught in the shallows.

reports.title: Lake Catherine Tailwater (Below Carpenter Dam) fishing report
reports.text: March also promises the beginning of the crappie spawn, which will add another quality game fish for the public to target.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Charles fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are good now on soft plastic worms and jigs. White bass continue to show up in good numbers and are biting jigs and worms. Crappie are good on worms and all color of jigs. Bream are good on worms and jigs. Shelly reports that the water temperature Monday was back up to 58.9 degrees The water level remains high and the clarity is the usual murky. The “moon” times indicate good days coming up this week (March 22-28), she says. The total eclipse in April should have a moon effect on the fishing the following month, with best days in April forecast for April 5-11 (the eclipse is April 8). Lake Charles might be a nice place from which to watch it, and catch some fish at the same time…

reports.title: Lake Maumelle fishing report
reports.text:
Kentucky bass (spotted bass) are great. People fishing for crappie are catching them as well.
Largemouth bass are still fair. Many report largemouths in prespawn mode and being found in 2-8 feet of water. Try using jigs, Alabama rigs, crankbaits and swimbaits, and try jerkbaits in shallow water during the afternoons.
Crappie are fair. They are at 8-12 feet. They are catching around brush piles but it’s a tough bite. Use jigs and minnows.

reports.title: Norfork Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Bass fishing is the best part way back in the creeks, and several are being caught. More crappie are showing up under docks back in the creeks, but not a lot. Blackburn’s has several guests in bass fishing and they report doing well and are satisfied with the bite.

reports.text: Donna Mulherin at Herman’s Landing ( 501-626-6899) reports that anglers are doing very well on crappie. The crappie are starting to get on their beds.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Maumelle fishing report
reports.text:
As for black bass, the largemouth bass are fair, while the spotted bass (Kentucky bass) are great. Largemouth bass are reported to be in prespawn and starting to spawn and can be found in 2-8 feet depth. Spotted bass are found around brush in 8-12 feet as well as in shallow water.
Crappie are fair. Some reports of the crappie being found 8-12 feet off points. Other reports of crappie being found around brush, but it’s a tough bite. Use jigs or minnows.

reports.title: Peckerwood Lake fishing report
reports.text: Donna Mulherin at Herman’s Landing ( 501-626-6899) reports that anglers are doing well on crappie. The crappie are starting to get on their beds, anglers say.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Arkansas River fishing report
reports.text: The University of Arkansas at Pine Bluff Bass Fishing Team reports that water temperature is in the mid-60s. Black bass are biting fairly well on bladed jigs, spinnerbaits, shallow-diving crankbaits, lipless crankbaits and creature baits/jigs around typical prespawn rocky banks and wooden cover. Some bass are positioned along the first sand drops away from spawning areas.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: DeGray Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Male buck bass were noted swimming through the shallow water. In a bass tournament over the weekend, the biggest bass caught topped 9 pounds, and then it fell off to the 6 pound range from there.
You’re going to want to fish weedless in the shallow areas as bass begin to hit those spots in their run-up to spawning.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Greeson fishing report
reports.text:
Southwest regional AGFC Fisheries biologists recently completed black bass spring electrofishing at Lake Greeson, capturing over 300 bass during their spring sampling effort, and fish appeared to be in good condition. They will conduct another black bass electrofishing effort this fall in order to evaluate fish condition going into the winter.
The biologists also offer this hot tip on Greeson: Bass are currently in about 6-10 feet of water near steep-sloping, rocky shorelines, and also on brush piles near shorelines.
Electrofishing is the most common sampling method for collecting data on black bass populations in Arkansas reservoirs.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nimrod fishing report
reports.text:
Crappie are biting well on minnows and jigs. White bass are good, but Sheila said the guys out crappie fishing are the ones catching white bass on the same baits for crappie.
Black bass are biting on spinnerbaits and jigs.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Arkansas River (Little Rock Area Pools) fishing report
reports.text: Fish ’N Stuff (501-834-5733) said the river backwaters are going to be the place to be right now for bass fishing. Also in the backwaters for bass, three-eighth-ounce jigs in black and blue are a good call with a crawfish trailer on it also in black and blue.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Beaver Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Crappie are starting to move shallower each week. Crappie are still suspended at different levels of the water column, and that seems to change lately for all you forward-facing sonar people. Crappie are also on brush and laydowns in 5-15 feet of water.
Bass are starting their pre-stage spawning and can be caught on jerkbaits off main lake and secondary points.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Craig D. Campbell Lake Conway Reservoir fishing report
reports.text:
Crappie continue to bite very well, and all the major species were biting well as the lake continues to fall out. Minnows and all colors of jigs are bringing in the crappie. A crankbait will work for black bass.
The pond is more than 60 acres and has bass, crappie, bream and stocked rainbow trout.
reports.lake: Craig D. Campbell Lake Conway Reservoir

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Greers Ferry Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Fish ’N Stuff (501-834-5733) in Sherwood says the bass are still beginning in the creeks on mid-diving crankbaits like the Rock Crawler in any orange or red color.
Crappie are roaming around chewing or roaming among pole timber or in brush piles — in all places they are suspended 4 feet down to 40 feet. Black bass are good super shallow out to 50 feet in guts, main lake points or secondary points and are biting on Alabama rigs, Carolina rigs, jerkbaits, football heads or crankbaits.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Charles fishing report
reports.text:
Bream and crappie are both biting well now, and the white bass have made a big appearance with good results. Black bass and catfish remain undetected for now.
Crappie like the jigs and worms as well.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Maumelle fishing report
reports.text:
Kentucky bass (spotted bass) are great. People fishing for crappie are catching them as well.
Largemouth bass are still fair. Reports of the largemouths in prespawn mode and being found in 2-8 feet of water. Try using jigs, Alabama rigs, crankbaits and swimbaits, and try jerkbaits in shallow water during the afternoons.
Crappie are good. They are at 12 feet and haven’t moved in shallow yet. They are catching around brush piles. Use jigs and minnows.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ouachita fishing report
reports.text:
Todd Gadberry at Mountain Harbor Resort and Spa (870-867-2191/800-832-2276 out-of-state) said black bass are excellent. Crappie are very good.
Darryl Morris of Family Fishing Trips (501-844-5418) said the Lake Ouachita crappie and black bass are beginning their spawn.
In the BLF tournament on Saturday, first place (Brice Boatwright) caught 18 pounds, 12 ounces; Chris Darby took second with 18-9, and the big bass was 6 pounds, by Grand Ford. Bass of Arkansas, first place, Derrick Sandlin catches 22.95 pounds, Trent Owens is second at 20.15 pounds and Brandon Rhoden has 19.43 AND a 10.62-pound Big Bass.
Bass anglers could fish by themselves and didn’t have to deal with someone else in the…

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Millwood Lake fishing report
reports.text:
* Largemouth bass have drastically improved activity over the past two weeks. Bass Assassin 5-inch Shads, plastic lizards, Brush Hogs, Tubes and spinnerbaits will draw a reaction in 2- to 6-feet depths. Hammer Traps, MR-6 and Echo 1.75, and Bill Lewis SB-57 MDJ crankbaits have all been getting random reaction bites over the past couple weeks from these active roaming bass in the deeper sections of creek channels or drops from the flats into 8-12 feet structure with stumps present. We caught good numbers of males the past two weeks on the Bass Assassin Shads, as well as lizards and spinnerbaits this week, in the shallow grass and buckbrush.
The largemouths’ reaction bites continue to be much…

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Norfork Lake fishing report
reports.text:
You cannot count on it and they are mostly bass and carp. The topwater bite for red meat fish and bass should be in full swing by April 15.
Keri landed two nice striped bass and a really good largemouth bass.
Joe was back at finding and catching some really nice walleye, crappie and one striped bass.
Crappie are staging for their spawn, which should happen before long. There are quite a few big slab crappie on or near brush piles back in creeks. The bass are still a little way off for their spawn, but with the early warm weather it might be sooner than normal.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Harris Brake Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Harris Brake Lake Resort (501-889-2745) says the bass and catfish are very active around the lake now.
Recently, a local bass fishing tournament posted good results with some really nice largemouths being caught, they report. The winning two-person team caught a 15-pound bag of fish (limit of five), and the tournament’s Big Bass catch was 3.7 pounds among the 16 boats competing.
Wednesday morning, a crappie angler was having good success catching fish in shallow water from his boat. The crappie appear to be moving closer to the shoreline for spawning. No bream have been reported lately.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Poinsett fishing report
reports.text: Bass and crappie are just starting to get into the prespawn. With the bass, you should have luck with frogs coming off water rose and lily pads. Crappie seem to be biting best on minnows around 10 feet of water, but you may do well with pink, green or Electric Blue jigs.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Little Maumelle River fishing report
reports.text:
Black bass are biting in 2-3 feet of water, and the females are full of eggs and up on the banks. It’s pretty much the same thing with the crappie, with the biting going on in 3 feet of water and they are obviously ready to spawn.
Among the crappie being caught, many are big now, particularly the females, he said.
Bass are biting on spinnerbaits, soft plastic worms and crankbaits.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Erling fishing report
reports.text:
Lake Erling Guide Service (870-904-8546) reports that crappie are biting really well and anglers were bringing in good fish topping 2 pounds.
Also some good black bass have also been caught.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Overcup fishing report
reports.text: Bass are getting ready to spawn. Crappie are being caught with minnows and jigs.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Chicot fishing report
reports.text: Crappie reports have been good from AGFC staffers in recent weeks. Anglers putting in from the Connerly Bayou Access have been seeing good results. Recent electrofishing surveys of the same area of Lake Chicot have revealed several crappie in the surveys. Lake Chicot, part of Lake Chicot State Park, is home to bluegill, channel catfish, largemouth bass, hybrid striped bass, redear sunfish and other bream, in addition to crappie. If you fish Lake Chicot, Connerly Bayou downstream of Connerly Dam, or Ditch Bayou from Lake Chicot downstream to Ditch Bayou Dam, be aware that crappie shorter than 10 inches must be immediately released and that the crappie daily limit is 20.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Millwood Lake fishing report
reports.text: * With elevation back on a slow rise, reduced current in Little River, and drastically improved clarity, we are seeing a few largemouth bass males and females roaming in areas of 1-6 feet depth around creeks, ridges and bedding flats on warm afternoons, near creek channel swings and vertical structure. Hammer Traps and MR-6, Echo 1.75 and Bill Lewis SB-57 MDJ crankbaits have all been getting random reaction bites over the past couple weeks from these active, roaming bass. Anywhere a creek channel is close by to the deeper creek bends or vertical structure and drops into the oxbows, where stumps are present, and where creek mouths drop, have held some decent-sized bass over the past several…

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Arkansas River (Little Rock Area Pools) fishing report
reports.text: You will locate black bass in better numbers in the backwaters, so target grass and wood in any kind of backwater you can get into.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Craig D. Campbell Lake Conway Reservoir fishing report
reports.text:
Bates Field and Stream (501-470-1846) said crappie continue to bite very well, and all the major species were biting well this week, as the lake continues to fall out.
Minnows and all colors of jigs are bringing in the crappie. A crankbait will work for black bass.
The pond is more than 60 acres and has bass, crappie, bream and stocked rainbow trout.
reports.lake: Craig D. Campbell Lake Conway Reservoir

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: DeGray Lake fishing report
reports.text:
The crappie are definitely moving up shallower and in transition to spawn.
(updated 2-22-2024) Black bass measuring 11.02 and 12.6 pounds were taken on successive weekends at DeGray at the end of January and early February by area anglers.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Greers Ferry Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Some crappie are roaming around chewing while others are doing the same in pole timber or in brush piles. Black bass are good super shallow out to 50 feet in guts, main lake points or secondary points.
Anglers are having success catching black bass on Damiki rigs with 3- to 4-inch Yamamoto Scope Shad.
In the creeks, anglers are catching bass on spinnerbaits and Chatterbait.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Harris Brake Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Harris Brake Lake Resort (501-889-2745) says some folks have been catching crappie out in deeper water in boats, but not from the shoreline. The fishing may be a little better now for black bass, and the occasional white bass, with some success off the shoreline.
But overall, they report, the amount of folks out fishing has been low; they seem to be waiting for warmer temperatures and for the crappie to move closer to the shoreline.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Catherine Tailwater (Below Carpenter Dam) fishing report
reports.text:
March also promises the beginning of the crappie spawn, which will add another quality game fish for the public to target.
The rising water does not affect the walleye and crappie bite to the same degree.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Charles fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on white/yellow jigs, as well as minnows. Black bass have done well lately, with good catches on spinnerbaits and soft plastic worms, as well as jigs.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Erling fishing report
reports.text:
Lake Erling Guide Service (870-904-8546) had no new reports, but it’s most recent news was that crappie were biting really well and anglers were bringing in good fish topping 2 pounds.
Also some good black bass have also been caught.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Maumelle fishing report
reports.text:
Largemouth bass are fair. Reports of the bass in prespawn mode and being found in 2-8 feet of water. Kentucky bass (spotted bass) also are fair.
Crappie are fair. There are reports of crappie moving in shallow in prespawn and they are about to start stacking. Target anywhere form 8-12 feet, and use jigs and minnows.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ouachita fishing report
reports.text:
Todd Gadberry at Mountain Harbor Resort and Spa (870-867-2191/800-832-2276 out-of-state) said black bass are excellent.
Crappie are fair.
The crappie are definitely moving up shallower and in transition to spawn.
In the BLF tournament on Saturday, first place (Brice Boatwright) caught 18 pounds, 12 ounces; Chris Darby took second with 18-9, and the big bass was 6 pounds, by Grand Ford. Bass of Arkansas, first place, Derrick Sandlin catches 22.95 pounds, Trent Owens is second at 20.15 pounds and Brandon Rhoden has 19.43 AND a 10.62-pound Big Bass.
Bass anglers could fish by themselves and didn’t have to deal with someone else in the boat, a definite advantage to moving around and hitting…

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Little Maumelle River fishing report
reports.text:
Both crappie and black bass are doing really well now. Crappie seem to be looking like they’re close to spawning, and in the Little Maumelle that usually happens when the temperature hits about 65 degrees, so a few warmer days after this current cold front that was passing through Wednesday-Thursday should get the water to that level.
Crappie are at about 3-4 feet and are wanting both minnows and jigs.
Black bass are showing up even shallower than the crappie, he said, with crankbaits, lizards and other soft plastics working well.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Norfork Lake fishing report
reports.text:
My barometer is when the bluegill, crappie and turtles move under my dock and they did it today.
“I first landed three striped bass, then they seemed to vacate the area, but the largemouth started to bite. Then the largemouth stopped biting and the hybrids took over. The hybrids took off and the largemouth started again.
One of our current guests, Joe, arrived Monday and has been crappie fishing. The crappie were suspended 20-30 feet deep on the top or inside of brush back in creeks.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Spring River fishing report
reports.text: Our bass love them, too.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Bull Shoals Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Bass fishing has been up and down with the weather fronts and changing daily.
Not much has changed with the crappie, and the crappie fishing is still pretty good. Crappie are still actively feeding and posting up on brush in the creeks.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: DeGray Lake fishing report
reports.text: The crappie are definitely moving up shallower and in transition to spawn.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Horseshoe Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Crappie are moving up in the water column and feeding heavily on shad. Watch the weather and as the temperature fluctuates, adjust your depth as the crappie will be moving with the temperature.
Still no report on black bass, and Kent says he’s not seen anyone bass fishing on the days he was out.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fayetteville fishing report
reports.text:
Crappie, black bass, white bass and even some carp are biting well.
Minnows are beginning to work well on crappie. Just about everything a black bass likes is working for them.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Arkansas River fishing report
reports.text: The University of Arkansas at Pine Bluff Bass Fishing Team had no new reports this week.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Arkansas River (Little Rock Area Pools) fishing report
reports.text: Bass are going to be shallow now, pretty close to the bank, with the water warming and with the sun shining. Anglers were also seeking bass by throwing a 3.5 black/red Gitzit Tube, flipping it along the bank and fishing it slowly.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Beaver Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Spotted bass are still good on Alabama rigs and jerkbaits. Crappie are on the move to the banks and will really start after this next week of warm weather.
Crappie are in prespawn mode but are being seen around cover and channel edges, and the fishing is pretty good for them as well.
They aren’t spawning yet (whites and crappie) but the fish have been actively feeding, so we’ve had good reports.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Craig D. Campbell Lake Conway Reservoir fishing report
reports.text: Bates Field and Stream (501-470-1846) said crappie are starting to pick up on jigs and minnows. Now that the water is warming up, the black bass are picking back up too.
reports.lake: Craig D. Campbell Lake Conway Reservoir

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: DeGray Lake fishing report
reports.text:
The largemouth and spots caught were keeper size but not really big fish – mostly male bass moving up to prepare the spawning beds. Bass were caught in 1-5 feet of water but closer to the deeper water. The bigger bass are probably holding deeper in those secondary points or in the great new coontail sitting in 9-15 feet of water.
In the BFL tournament held here on Saturday, tourney anglers had several five-bass limits of bass beginning to come up the shallower water, but most weren’t made up of really big fish. First place was almost 19 pounds, second place was 13 pounds and a large number of anglers were in the 6- to 8-pound range among the five keeper bass.
Sunday, the crappie anglers…

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Greers Ferry Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Crappie will likely be found around brush and vegetation near the old shoreline as they were moving up to spawn when the last rise of water came into the system. Vertical jigging a crappie tube on a one-sixteenth-ounce ball-headed jig using at least a 10-foot jigging pole would be a good approach.
Some black bass are eating jerkbaits, crankbaits and spinnerbaits in guts or side of guts. Some crappie are as shallow as a couple of feet, while most are 10-40 feet.
Also, a floating worm and a Senko thrown around the bushes will work at picking up black bass.
They have not heard any reports on crappie with the lake coming up so high.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Charles fishing report
reports.text:
Shelly Jeffrey at Lake Charles State Park (870-878-6595) said crappie fishing picked up significantly this past week. The crappie catches were good, with anglers using white and chartreuse jigs fished right off the shoreline. No reports were received on black bass or white bass.
The water temperature took a big jump in a week, which correlated with the crappie bite.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Maumelle fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass fishing is good. Reports have come in of bass being found both deep and in shallow sports along rocky points. Some reports say they are deep, 18-22 feet. Try using Carolina-rigged lizards, crankbaits, spinnerbait and drop-shots. Kentucky bass (spotted bass) are also biting well. Some reports have them being found near drop-offs around 16-20 feet and off rocky banks, and other reports say they are being found on brush piles. Try using a Texas rig on brush, or use a jig.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ouachita fishing report
reports.text:
Darryl Morris of Family Fishing Trips (501-844-5418) said the water temp is perfect for the beginning of the crappie and bass spawn. “We’ve been catching ample numbers of crappie and bass on staging brush piles with jigs and minnows fished 6-12 feet deep.”
(updated 3-23-2023) Todd Gadberry at Mountain Harbor Resort and Spa (870-867-2191/800-832-2276 out-of-state) said black bass are still good. Crappie are very good on small jigs or minnows.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Millwood Lake fishing report
reports.text: * Largemouth and spotted bass have been staging for several weeks near creek channels and dumps into Little River and the oxbow. Some males from 2-3 pounds were found shallow in 1-3 feet of water on flats near vegetation, and others in 6- to 9-foot deep creek channels where grass and reeds and fresh lily pad shoots are emerging, on Brazalo spinnerbaits, lizards, brush hogs and Bass Assassins. Over the past couple weeks, largemouths have been randomly feeding in creek channels dumping into Little River. A few chunky 2 and 3 pound male Bass, were the most aggressive at mid day into late afternoon over the past couple weeks and those fish we are finding randomly near and close to deeper creek…

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Norfork Lake fishing report
reports.text:
“Fishing has not been the best but a few bass are being caught beating the bank partway back in the creeks with a red crankbait or a single spin. I am using a small grub tipped with a minnow almost exclusively and catching a few bass and a crappie now and again.
“Overall fishing is poor but some bass are being caught if you know how.
“You can catch just about any species in the lake, including walleye, crappie and stripers, by casting out a swimbait.
Bob, another guest, found nice largemouth bass back in a creek in very shallow, muddy water.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Harris Brake Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Harris Brake Lake Resort (501-889-2745) says crappie remains slow.
Largemouth bass fishing has been really good, with one angler landing a 4.5-pound fish (21 inches in length) on a spinnerbait.
If you’re going for crappie, the boat anglers are trying in the shallow area now with minnows and with a Crappie Stinger jig. Spinnerbaits and bass minnows are what are working for the bass.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Little Maumelle River fishing report
reports.text:
Some anglers were out catching really nice crappie, Ray said, landing them in 3 feet depth on minnows.
Black bass also have been doing really well. Several people landed bass this week using Alabama rigs, crankbaits, worms – basically catching them on everything, Ray said.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Brewer Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Anglers say 12-15 feet is where you’ll find the catchable crappie. Crappie like the live stuff, but will also go for jigs in chartreuse/white or Electric Chicken.
Black bass are starting to hit on the warm days, though David admits they haven’t really had many warm days yet. Bass are not up in the shallow water yet like they would typically be in the summertime. Bass will eat minnows now as well.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Crown Lake fishing report
reports.text: Boxhound Marina (870-670-4496) has seen some activity with bass being caught in good numbers and are reported to be healthy “and chunky.” No bass are on top yet, but they are moving into shallower areas. They’ve seen some crappie anglers out.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Dardanelle fishing report
reports.text:
The bass spawn has started. Some people have been catching bass on spinnerbaits “but I have not been able to get that accomplished.
Crappie are kind of scattered; some are still deep, with some extremely shallow. I have noticed the creeks with a lot of stumps have the crappie up pretty shallow on the stumps. But in places that don’t have stumps and they have brush, the crappie could be as deep as 10 feet, but we’re seeing a lot of them suspended in the trees at 5 feet. In the deep creek, some of the crappie are down as deep as 20 feet.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Hamilton fishing report
reports.text: Darryl Morris of Family Fishing Trips (501-844-5418) said for all the lakes he fishes in the Hot Springs area – DeGray, Hamilton and Ouachita – the water temp is perfect for the beginning of the crappie and bass spawn. “We’ve been catching ample numbers of crappie and bass on staging brush piles with jigs and minnows fished 6-12 feet deep.”

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Bull Shoals Lake fishing report
reports.text:
The bass have been stingy the last couple of days.
The bass are definitely grouping up.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Beaver Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Crappie are fair and are very scattered.
Black bass are hitting jerkbaits and Alabama rigs on points that lead back into many of the arms from mid-lake on toward the Dam.
Crappie are in prespawn mode abut are being seen around cover and channel edges, and the fishing is pretty good for them as well.
They aren’t spawning yet (whites and crappie) but the fish have been actively feeding, so we’ve had good reports.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Brewer Lake fishing report
reports.text:
A local bass tournament last weekend didn’t even have a limit weighted in. They did have a 6.5-pounder weighed in for Big Bass.
Crappie reports have been poor as well. In about 40 angler hours as reported in the creel survey, there may have been 1 crappie and 3 bass caught on Thursday, he says.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Buffalo National River/Crooked Creek fishing report
reports.text: With cooler temperatures, the smallmouths have not been active.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Craig D. Campbell Lake Conway Reservoir fishing report
reports.text:
Crappie are slow. They’re biting on the typical catfish bait, with a real interest for trotline minnows, crappie minnows and goldfish.
Black bass are doing really well.
reports.lake: Craig D. Campbell Lake Conway Reservoir

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: DeGray Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Randy Plyler with Plyler Outdoors Guide Service (870-210-0522) said bass fishing has been up and down this past week with the weather changing from cold to warm conditions. Bass are being caught on a Carolina rig as well as jerkbaits and spinnerbaits. Crappie are moving up to shallower brush piles and can be caught on jigs and live bait.
Crappie are moving up into the brush piles. “We’ve been catching crappie on live bait 8-12 feet deep on brush piles in 16-24 feet of water.”

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Greers Ferry Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Black bass are eating jerkbaits, crankbaits and spinnerbaits in guts or side of guts. Some crappie are as shallow as a couple of feet, while most are 10-40 feet – jigs, minnows or crankbaits are catching them.
They are throwing crankbaits, single swimbaits and also a Carolina rig for the bass.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Charles fishing report
reports.text: Nothing was reported on crappie, black bass or catfish.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Dardanelle fishing report
reports.text: Crappie have pushed back out to deeper water. A large amount of bass has been pushed back, also. You can still catch quite a few buck bass in the shallows, but the big females are out in deeper water, waiting to move back shallow.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Maumelle fishing report
reports.text:
Black bass fishing is good. Fishing on Thursday morning on a windy point was working well for black bass. Crappie fishing is slow.
This Wednesday afternoon the lake was too dirty on the west end for some anglers looking for any white bass there, and they didn’t do any good outside of catching a few black bass.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ouachita fishing report
reports.text:
Todd Gadberry at Mountain Harbor Resort and Spa (870-867-2191/800-832-2276 out-of-state) said black bass are still good. Crappie are very good on small jigs or minnows.
Darryl Morris of Family Fishing Trips (501-844-5418) said crappie are moving up into the brush piles. “We’ve been catching crappie on live bait 8-12 feet deep on brush piles in 16-24 feet of water,” he said.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Millwood Lake fishing report
reports.text:
* Largemouth and spotted bass have been staging for several weeks near creek channels and dumps into Little River; however, high flow conditions in Little River make river fishing somewhat difficult to maintain.
Over the past couple weeks, largemouths were randomly feeding in creek channels dumping into Little River. A few chunky 2- and 3-pound male bass were the most aggressive at midday into late afternoon recently and those fish were randomly near deeper creek channels hitting Brazalo Spinnerbaits in Spot Remover, Chatterbaits in Firecraw or black and blue and Rat-L-Traps in Red Chrome Crawfish, Millwood Magic or Toledo Gold.
Bass Assassin Shads in Pumpkinseed, Houdini and Chico’s Red…

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nimrod fishing report
reports.text:
Andrews Bait Shop and More (479-272-4025) says that the crappie anglers with LiveScope are catching their 30 “but it’s kinda tough out here right now.”
The bream aren’t reporting on Nimrod, and the black bass aren’t taking even to the reliable-on-Nimrod War Eagle Spinnerbait.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Bull Shoals Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Bass fishing is up and down like the weather; there are some fish moving up.
The bass are definitely grouping up if you can find them.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Norfork Lake fishing report
reports.text:
“You can catch just about any species in the lake, including walleye, crappie and stripers, by casting out a swimbait.
Bob, another guest, found nice largemouth bass back in a creek in very shallow, muddy water.
Trollers are catching a few temperate bass dragging live bait and umbrellas through shad and others are casting artificial lures back in the bayous and bays.
“ Crappie fishing on brush is not the best, but a few fish are being caught every day. Shad are moving under docks under lights about 9 p.m. and bringing spawned out white bass and walleye and a few crappie with them. Some bass are back in the creeks near the shore, but not a lot.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Buffalo National River/Crooked Creek fishing report
reports.text:
With cooler temperatures, the smallmouths have not been active.
Spotted bass are doing well on points back in the major arms on jerkbaits and Alabama rigs.
Crappie are in prespawn mode abut are being seen around cover and channel edges, and the fishing is pretty good for them as well.
They aren’t spawning yet (whites and crappie) but the fish have been actively feeding, so we’ve had good reports.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: DeGray Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Randy Plyler with Plyler Outdoors Guide Service (870-210-0522) said this past Saturday there were a lot of bass caught by the young guns in the high school tournament held here. Lot of five-fish limits were caught, including an 8.01-pound largemouth bass weighed in.
Bass can be caught on crankbaits as well as bladed jigs, jigs and shaky heads. Crappie are moving up and are grouping and can be caught on jigs, so watch your LiveScope for them.
Crappie are moving up into the brush piles. “We’ve been catching crappie on live bait 8-12 feet deep on brush piles in 16-24 feet of water.”

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Greers Ferry Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Black bass are eating jerkbaits, crankbaits and spinnerbaits in guts or side of guts; the rest are out deeper and can be caught dragging something, and some are right up on shoreline.
Some crappie are as shallow as a couple of feet.
(updated 3-2-2023) Fish ’N Stuff (501-834-5733) in Sherwood said the fish are pushing toward the back of creeks, and most of the black bass reported caught have been hauled in from the middle to the backs of creeks this week.
For crappie, anglers have been catching lot of fish around the South Fork River and up around Choctaw.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Charles fishing report
reports.text:
Shelly Jeffrey at Lake Charles State Park (870-878-6595) said white and black crappie are hitting jigs (black, Monkey Milk, chartreuse/red and Bleeding Shad are the best colors now).
Black bass are fair at best, and catfish and white bass weren’t reported. Shelly says, “We have nightcrawlers, crickets, jigs and lures, and poles. Stop by and see us at the Visitors Center for all your tackle needs.” The lake’s temperature still tends to lean toward the low 50s; it was 51.9 degrees on Monday. The level is high and the lake is its usual murky clarity.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Hamilton fishing report
reports.text:
Crappie are moving up into the brush piles. “We’ve been catching crappie on live bait 8-12 feet deep on brush piles in 16-24 feet of water.”
(updated 3-2-2023) Fish ’N Stuff (501-834-5733) in Sherwood said that with the water warming up, black bass are moving toward the backs of the creeks or toward spawning flats.
Crappie have been hanging around those 15-foot brush pile in the creeks, the guts of creeks and pockets.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ouachita fishing report
reports.text: Todd Gadberry at Mountain Harbor Resort and Spa (870-867-2191/800-832-2276 out-of-state) said b lack bass are good.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Poinsett fishing report
reports.text: Seth Boone, the superintendent at Lake Poinsett State Park, reported Lake Poinsett’s crappie biting well on minnows and jigs. Bass are starting to bite on artificials off of the points. Crappie and bass are catch-and-release at Lake Poinsett.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Millwood Lake fishing report
reports.text:
*Big, fat, prespawn female largemouths came out to play this past week. Over the past couple weeks black bass have been randomly feeding along Little River and the oxbows, with a few warmer days over the past couple weeks being best days to make a run upriver. A few chunky 2- and 3-pound male bass were most aggressive at midday into late afternoon over the past few weeks and those fish are randomly near and close to deeper creek channels. The best water clarity, and reaction from chunky largemouths, has left the river and moved to the back of the oxbows like McGuire, Clear Lake and Horseshoe Lake where the clarity is somewhat better away from the current of Little River.
Bass Assassin Shads…

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Norfork Lake fishing report
reports.text: Some crappie are on main lake shallow brush and partway in the backs of creeks on any wood.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: White River fishing report
reports.text: An added bonus of fishing in the creeks is the chance to catch a nice smallmouth bass.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Erling fishing report
reports.text:
Anglers are catching a lot of crappie now, and lot of those crappie are in the 2-pounds-plus range. Bright-colored jigs are the way to go, and hand-tied jigs are doing the best, but quite a few crappie have been caught on minnows also.
Bass anglers aren’t letting on to what they’re using, but they appear to be bringing in a lot of bass as well. One regular angler had a five-bass stringer that weighed 20 pounds Wednesday.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Hamilton fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are moving up into the brush piles. “We’ve been catching crappie on live bait 8-12 feet deep on brush piles in 16-24 feet of water.”

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Little Maumelle River fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are doing well and being caught in 4-5 feet depth. Black bass are doing real well, also, and they’re being caught in the same depth of water.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Erling fishing report
reports.text:

Bass anglers aren’t letting on to what they’re using, but they appear to be bringing in a lot of bass as well. One regular angler had a five-bass stringer that weighed 20 pounds Wednesday.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fayetteville fishing report
reports.text: Lake Fayetteville Boat Dock (479-444-3476) said crappie are doing really well on jigs. Black bass are biting on craws and soft plastics, and there has also been some topwater action lately.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Bull Shoals Lake fishing report
reports.text:
If you’re bass fishing, fish the conditions.
The smallmouth bass are definitely grouping up; if you can find them they are in packs!

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Beaver Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Spotted bass have ramped up on jerkbaits in the backs of Rambo, Clifty and Joe’s and Blackburn arms. Crappie are really scattered and moving into main arms and starting to stage up on brush adjacent to known spawning areas. With the rise of water do not be afraid to look shallow for both crappie and bass.
Crappie are rated fair to good. There are not a lot of crappie anglers out yet with the chill (35 degrees Friday) still in the air. The crappie are in a prespawn bite and found around brush and other cover. Many crappie anglers are using the LiveScope and searching them out and using a variety of baits, mostly jigs, artificials and minnows.
Black bass are still in a winter pattern and that…

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Buffalo National River/Crooked Creek fishing report
reports.text: With warmer temperatures, the smallmouths should be soon active.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Craig D. Campbell Lake Conway Reservoir fishing report
reports.text:
Anglers going to Gold Creek are still catching a few crappie. When closed, the lake starts clearing up and settling better, which crappie anglers like.
Other than the crappie, they had heard nothing else this week.
In the past couple of weeks though, bass anglers were out getting ready for tournaments with topwater lures, Chatterbaits, buzzbaits, worms, shad-type flukes, creature baits and swimbaits.
One angler had a good day catching a 4.4-pound largemouth and seven crappie, returning all those back to the water.
reports.lake: Craig D. Campbell Lake Conway Reservoir

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: DeGray Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Bass have moved into a prespawn pattern and have moved into waters 1-10 feet deep.
Crappie have moved up and have been bunched up.
Whites bass are running can be caught on lipless crankbaits or shad-colored crankbaits.
Water is warming and the crappie are moving up to their staging brush piles.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Greers Ferry Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Black bass are eating jerkbaits, crankbaits and spinnerbaits in guts or side of guts; the rest are out deeper and can be caught dragging something and some are right up on shoreline. Some crappie are as shallow as a couple of feet, while most are 10-40 feet.

For crappie, anglers have been catching lot of fish around the South Fork River and up around Choctaw.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Charles fishing report
reports.text: Crappie had picked up but maybe fell off just a little to fair this past week. Black bass are still fair, but Shelly didn’t have report on baits used.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Hamilton fishing report
reports.text:
Water is warming and the crappie are moving up to their staging brush piles.

Crappie have been hanging around those 15-foot brush pile in the creeks, the guts of creeks and pockets.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ouachita fishing report
reports.text:
Todd Gadberry at Mountain Harbor Resort and Spa (870-867-2191/800-832-2276 out-of-state) said black bass are still good. Crappie are good on small jigs or minnows.
Water is warming and the crappie are moving up to their staging brush piles.

The best water clarity and reaction from chunky bass have left the river and moved to the back of McGuire, Clear Lake and Horseshoe Lake oxbows…

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Norfork Lake fishing report
reports.text:
“ Crappie fishing picked up and then has slowed again and bass fishing is pretty good.
Trollers are catching a variety of fish dragging umbrellas through shad; brush fishing is fair for Kentucky bass and crappie, people beating the bank back in the creeks, and others casting jigs and small grubs over brush and letting them sink into it are all catching fish.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Spring River fishing report
reports.text:
“A few browns have been caught lately but mainly good rainbows and smallmouth.
The smallmouth have been hitting lately on deep slow presentations. Sink tips with snag free flies work well. Minnow and sculpins patterns are the fav, with crawfish patterns working well too somedays. Got to get it down! With river levels up, be safe wading; a wading staff can save a life. The Spring River has a very slick river bottom that is hard to wade normally, so be careful. With the public areas getting a lot of pressure, places like Riverside Resort that is open through the winter can offer better wading and less pressure. All of the campgrounds will open April 1, providing more accesses. And stocking…

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Arkansas River fishing report
reports.text: The University of Arkansas at Pine Bluff Bass Fishing Team reports water temperatures in low 60s mostly with upper 60s in protected backwaters. Black bass are biting fairly well on small dark-colored jigs and soft plastics. Black bass are transitioning into traditional spawning areas but have not quite loaded into them yet.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Harris Brake Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Crappie are still biting but it’s difficult to catch them from the shoreline or dock.
“People are fishing 5-foot deep for crappie.”

reports.title: Spring River fishing report
reports.text:
“A few browns have been caught lately but mainly good rainbows and smallmouth.
The smallmouth have been hitting lately on deep slow presentations. Sink tips with snag free flies work well. reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Horseshoe Lake fishing report
reports.text:
With the rising water and the rising temperatures one would think the crappie fishing would be on fire. The crappie are/were still deep and finicky.
“There was a bass tournament on Saturday (two tournaments, I think). Most folks I saw bass fishing were in the shallows.”

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Bull Shoals Lake fishing report
reports.text: The smallmouth are definitely grouping up if you can find them; they are in roaming mode.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Beaver Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair/good and are either on the bottom on flats adjacent to main channels or attached to brush in 10-20 feet of water. Black bass are loading up on prespawn areas. Look for point and humps with some structure. Jerkbaits and swimbaits will continue to shine. Walleye are in the river arms and will continue to stay in those areas until the spawn is over in a month or so. “We are expecting lots of rain in the next day with 2-4 inches forecast, and this will temporarily put a kink in the fishing, especially in the main tributaries that feed Beaver. I will tell you one overlooked fish to put in the boat with that type of rain is the catfish. This time of year with that kind of rain…

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Buffalo National River/Crooked Creek fishing report
reports.text: With warmer temperatures, the smallmouths should be active soon.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Craig D. Campbell Lake Conway Reservoir fishing report
reports.text:
One angler had a good day catching a 4.4-pound largemouth and seven crappie, returning all those back to the water.
(updated 2-23-2023) Bates Field and Stream (501-470-1846) said crappie have been biting in the usual hot spots like Gold Creek. Crappie were reported at about 6 feet depth in Gold Creek, and at 6-8 feet depth around the Highway 89 bridge area.
Bass anglers picking up topwater lures, Chatterbaits, buzzbaits, worms, shad-type flukes, creature baits and swimbaits.
reports.lake: Craig D. Campbell Lake Conway Reservoir

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Crown Lake fishing report
reports.text: Boxhound Marina (870-670-4496) has reopened for the fishing season and for the past three weeks they’ve started to see increasing activity, particularly out of the bass anglers. The bass being caught in good numbers are reported all healthy “and chunky.” No bass are on top yet, but they are moving in to shallower areas. They’ve seen some crappie anglers out, but so far there have been no reports.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Greers Ferry Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Crappie are scattered around all over water column eating jigs and jigs with minnow or trolled crankbaits in 5-50 feet. Black bass are about the same, but eating craws, jigs, crankbaits, Alabama rigs, spinnerbaits, traps or drag a Carolina rig or big football head super shallow out to 50 feet.
(updated 3-2-2023) Fish ’N Stuff (501-834-5733) in Sherwood said the fish are pushing toward the back of creeks, and most of the black bass reported caught have been hauled in from the middle to the backs of creeks this week.
For crappie, anglers have been catching lot of fish around the South Fork River and up around Choctaw.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Charles fishing report
reports.text:
Shelly Jeffrey at Lake Charles State Park (870-878-6595) said crappie have really picked up.
Black bass and catfish are fair, but anglers didn’t suggest any specific baits. Bream are no biting right yet. Neither are white bass. Shelly notes that the state park visitor center carries nightcrawlers, lures and jigs, and poles. Hours are 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. every day. The lake’s water temperature on Monday was 51.9 degrees. The lake is usually murky and the water is high.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Hamilton fishing report
reports.text:
Fish ’N Stuff (501-834-5733) in Sherwood said that with the water warming up, black bass are moving toward the backs of the creeks or toward spawning flats.
Crappie have been hanging around those 15-foot brush pile in the creeks, the guts of creeks and pockets.
