reports.title: Lake Ouachita fishing report
reports.text: Todd Gadberry at Mountain Harbor Resort and Spa (870-867-2191/800-832-2276 out-of-state) said black bass are good. Crappie are good on small jigs or minnows.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Millwood Lake fishing report
reports.text:
* Over the past couple weeks the largemouths and spotted bass have been randomly feeding along Little River and the oxbows, with the warmer days being best to make a run upriver. A few chunky 2- and 3-pound male bass were the most aggressive at midday into late afternoon and those fish were being found randomly near and close to deeper creek channels. The bass have randomly been hitting Brazalo Spinnerbaits in Spot Remover, Chatterbaits in white or Firecraw, and Rat-L-Traps in Red Chrome Crawfish, Millwood Magic or Toledo Gold.
Floating a Trick Worm like the Senko or Zoom Trick Worm and the Yum Dingers and Bass Assassin Shads is a pattern that’s beginning to get good reactions. Big female…

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Arkansas River (Little Rock Area Pools) fishing report
reports.text:
With warmer water temperatures, bass anglers should head toward the backwaters and fish shallower areas. Just try to target any visible cover where black bass are pulling up to spawn.
The crappie have been on the backwater holes on the inside of jetties in 10 feet of water. Crappie anglers are catching them on orange/chartreuse jigs and red/chartreuse and solid chartreuse crappie jigs.
(updated 3-2-2023) Hatchet Jack’s Sports Shop in Crystal Hill off I-40 (501-758-4958) said the river is slow on catfish for now, while crappie are “fair to middlin’” on jigs or minnows.
But some good days have happened lately with crappie, as one angler reported a limit of big 14- to-17-inch crappie caught in…

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Crown Lake fishing report
reports.text: Boxhound Marina (870-670-4496) has reopened for the fishing season and for the past three weeks they’ve started to see some activity, particularly out of the bass anglers. The bass being caught in good numbers are reported all healthy “and chunky.” No bass are on top yet, but they are moving in to shallower areas. They’ve seen some crappie anglers out, but so far there have been no reports.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Arkansas River (Little Rock Area Pools) fishing report
reports.text:
Bass are going to be shallow now, pretty close to the bank, with the water warming and with the sun shining.
Anglers also have been seeking bass by throwing a 3.5 black/red Gitzit Tube.
Guys and gals searching out the bass have been taking a spinnerbait in white/chartreuse out along the bank areas.
They haven’t heard any reports on crappie fishing this week, but those fish should be staging soon in 8-10 feet of water behind the jetties and likely located near wood or a drop-off. If you’re seeking the crappie, go with an orange/chartreuse, red/chartreuse or white/chartreuse crappie jig.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Bull Shoals Lake fishing report
reports.text: The smallmouth are definitely grouping up if you can find them.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Arkansas River fishing report
reports.text: The University of Arkansas at Pine Bluff Bass Fishing Team reported water temperatures are in the upper 50s to lower 60s on the main channel and within Lake Langhofer. Black bass are biting well and are in all phases of spawn (pre-, active, post-) right now.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Arkansas River (Little Rock Area Pools) fishing report
reports.text: (updated 3-31-2022) Zimmerman’s Exxon (501-944-2527) said crappie good in the backwaters on minnows and jigs.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Beaver Lake fishing report
reports.text:
“ Crappie are really good, as the prespawn bite is on. Some really big crappie for Beaver are being caught.
Black bass are good and staging near spawning areas.
Crappie are good on minnows and small jigs. Black bass are good on crankbaits, jerkbaits and jigs.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Brewer Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good and are still being caught in 6-8 feet depth. Black bass are good on jigs and anything white and spinning.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Clear Lake fishing report
reports.text: McSwain Sports Center (501-945-2471) said crappie anglers are doing well here. The bite is good on minnows and jigs, and some really good-sized crappie are being caught.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Cooks Lake fishing report
reports.text: The scenic lake is full of slab crappie, giant bluegills, largemouth bass, and catfish of all species.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Craig D. Campbell Lake Conway Reservoir fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good using pink minnows, rosy red minnows, or a jig. Black bass are good on spinnerbaits, buzzbaits, swimbaits, 7- to 10-inch curly tail worms and 6- and 8-inch Magnum Lizards.
reports.lake: Craig D. Campbell Lake Conway Reservoir

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Crown Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie fishing is good on the usual crappie baits. Black bass are good, though no baits were suggested (we can suggest spinnerbaits and jerkbaits here at this time, however).

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: DeGray Lake fishing report
reports.text: That means crappie and black bass are beginning their spawn.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Greers Ferry Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Black bass are eating a lot of baits right now.
Crappie are eating and moving and doing it all over again, from 10-40 feet.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Harris Brake Lake fishing report
reports.text: The recent inclement weather, including Wednesday’s cold front, has slowed down the crappie bite. Black bass are fair with the boating anglers, who are using minnows and crappie jigs.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Charles fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair on minnows, jigs and worms. Black bass are fair on plastic worms and topwater lures.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Erling fishing report
reports.text: Crappie picked back up. Black bass were schooling around the bridges and the bite has been fair.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fayetteville fishing report
reports.text: Crappie picked up again after the cold front with good results; use minnows and jigs. Black bass are good using crankbaits or plastic worms.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nimrod fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good. Black bass are fair.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ouachita fishing report
reports.text:
Todd Gadberry at Mountain Harbor Resort and Spa (870-867-2191/800-832-2276 out of state) said black bass are very good. Crappie are very good on small jigs or minnows.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Sequoyah fishing report
reports.text: Lake Sequoyah Boat Dock (479-444-3475) says walleye are good below the dam for anglers throwing white swimbaits or bass minnows. Crappie are fair using minnows or goldfish. Black bass are fair on spinnerbaits and crankbaits.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Little Maumelle River fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are biting well, especially at night on yo-yos. The crappie appear to be moving shallower. Black bass are good in 3-5 feet of water.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Millwood Lake fishing report
reports.text:
* The largemouth activities have been slowly getting better each week recently. Numerous male bass and a few fat prespawn females, continue to be found roaming flats from 2-6 feet deep where bedding areas exist, searching out new bedding sites. For the last 2-3 weeks, these roaming Largemouths have been quick to strike on Lizards, Brazalo Spinnerbaits, Chatterbaits, Trick Worms, Senkos, salty rat tails and Bass Assassin Shads.
The shallow cruising male Largemouth Bass we found roaming bedding areas over the past couple weeks, were around 2.5-3 pounds, and fairly spooky anywhere you can find the clear water, and continue moving in and out of 2-6′ deep flats with stumps and grass present near…

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Norfork Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Some male crappie have moved to the backs of creeks and are staging for spawn, but there has been no evidence of either bass or crappie making nests yet. I found some schools of crappie on main lake points on brush from 18-25 feet but it has been hard to stay on them in the wind.
“Bass are on the same brush but are on the bottom and they are mostly Kentucky bass.

I found crappie roaming around in the middle of a popular spawning pocket and was able to catch one as shallow as 6 feet.
It was full of eater-size crappie. There were also tons of hybrids there, too, which sometimes makes it hard to focus just on the crappie. By midday we had a pretty good mess of crappie as well as a mixed bag. Crappie Slab Slanger in Monkey Milk paired with an orange head worked slow, slow, slow.

reports.text:
* Largemouth bass began a slow improvement this week with the warmer conditions, depending on location. The largemouth prime activity and cycles have been best midday and afternoon. Several male bass have been found roaming flats from 2-6 feet deep where bedding areas exist, apparently searching out new bedding sites. As of late, those roaming male largemouths have been eager to strike on 1-knocker Rat-L-Traps in Millwood Magic, Gold, Toledo Gold and Goldfire Craw.
The male largemouth bass we found roaming shallow over the last week were around 2-2.5 pounds, and moving in and out of 3- to 6-feet deep flats with stumps present near creek channel drops from 4-9 feet deep, near vertical…

Crappie are in a prespawn pattern.

reports.text:
Best places to start searching for spawning crappie are small protected pockets along the main river channel and main creek channels.
Fishing for spawning crappie can sometimes be feast or famine depending on if you find where they are socializing. If you go back and review some locations in my winter reports and find the shallows in those areas you will find spawning crappie. Pick one of these areas and spend the entire day fishing the area thoroughly and you will find spawning crappie.

A white or pink jig and live minnow are working wonderfully in depths of 25 feet. Use caution when navigating the lake. reports.title: Bear Creek Lake/Storm Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Tyler Ball, park ranger at Mississippi River State Park (870-295-4040), said that at Bear Creek Lake, anglers report success in catching largemouth bass between depths of 4-6 feet within specific coves. Anglers are reporting catching those largemouths with various types of artificial baits.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Dardanelle fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing has picked up and they are starting to chase Chatterbaits, jigs, spinnerbaits, swimbaits, crankbaits and plastics. Crappie have improved a lot,with some quite shallow.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Arkansas River fishing report
reports.text: Bass are hit or miss, with best results coming on black/blue Chatterbait in the backwaters. Crappie have been good for anglers throwing orange/chartreuse, blue/chartreuse and black/chartreuse crappie jigs.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Beaver Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Crappie are good on brush in 10-20 feet of water.
Black bass are hitting A-rigs and jerkbaits throughout the lake.
Crappie are biting well in 10-15 feet depth, with anglers using minnows, jigs and crankbaits. Black bass are fair on Alabama rigs and jerkbaits.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Brewer Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Crappie fishing is good. The crappie are being found 15 feet deep. Crappie was all that was reported.
Before the winter weather fronts passed through, the word was that crappie are elusive and set up on the southwest end, favoring a drop-shot with small jigs. Bass were starting to show themselves along the grass.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Craig D. Campbell Lake Conway Reservoir fishing report
reports.text: Crappie reports have been fair; go with minnows and jigs. Bass are biting for anglers dropping jigs.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Greers Ferry Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Crappie will eat if you get bait in front of them in 18-40 feet of water in and around brushpiles, or pole timber, or just floating around the guts of deep pockets; use jigs and minnows. Bass are good with crankbaits, traps, spinnerbaits, jigs, hair jigs, jerkbaits and C-rigs from super shallow – some are even in bushes sunning – out to 60 feet.
Bass are pretty good on cloudy days using Alabama rigs and jerkbaits in 10-15 feet of water. Crappie are hit-and-miss these days, with popsicle color and Bobby Garland Jigs in monkey milk fished in 25 feet of water.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Harris Brake Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie fishing remains good. Crappie are still in the deeper areas and anglers are catching them with minnows and jigs. Bream are poor, as are bass.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Horseshoe Lake fishing report
reports.text:
For crappie, try spider-rigging in 18-25 feet of water 20 feet deep with minnows or jigs. As the water temperature continues to rise with warmer weather, expect the crappie to move up some in the water column. Also, look for schools of baitfish and the crappie should not be far away.
No reports on bass, bream or catfish this week.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fayetteville fishing report
reports.text: Anglers have returned and have caught a fair amount of crappie, using jigs. Black bass are fair; try crankbaits or even a topwater lure.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Hamilton fishing report
reports.text:
Bass fishing has been really good lately, even with all the up and down weather and rain. The most effective setups for bass have been the drop-shot rig with a wacky-rigged white or pink worm and dragged in 5 feet intervals on flats that are 25 feet deep and near current. The Ned rig fished vertically is still doing really well in green pumpkin or pink, but this will end soon as the water temps get to the 50-degree mark. A white spinnerbait slowly rolled along the bottom in shallower water depths of 12 feet or less has been doing well also. Not surprising that it has come into play as the fish are gearing up for pre-spawn.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Maumelle fishing report
reports.text:
The largemouth bass bite is slow. Kentucky bass (or spotted bass ) are also slow. There have been reports of them being found still mixed in with the crappie and are in transition.
Crappie are excellent. Some reports have surfaced this week of the crappie being found in the deeper part of the lake, around 45-50 feet. Try using jigs and minnows. No reports of any bream caught this week, but try using crickets and worms. Catfishing is fair. Chicken liver, worms and crayfish will work best now.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Monticello fishing report
reports.text:
* Largemouth bass: Bass were a little hungrier this week with warmer daytime highs and full sun. Brazalo Spinnerbaits in white/chartreuse, Millwood Mayhem Bream and Spot Remover caught a few more decent bass this week, and Chatterbaits picked up a few 2-3 pound largemouths this week.
“Most bass we are finding continue randomly roaming shallow on full sun and bright skies in the 3- to 6-foot depths of flats adjacent to deeper drops into 7-10 feet depth ranges,” Mike says. Anywhere a creek channel runs into the deeper creek bends or vertical structure and drops into the oxbows, where stumps and creek mouths drop, have held some decent-sized bass over the past few weeks.
Heavy thumper tail…

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Overcup fishing report
reports.text: The only real successful fishing now is for crappie. Poor reports for bass, bream and catfish.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Little Maumelle River fishing report
reports.text: Best reports have come from crappie anglers, who report a fair bite on minnows and jigs. Bream and black bass reports have been poor over the past week.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Beaver Tailwater fishing report
reports.text: As for the Kentucky bass, you need to fish more toward Beaver and Holiday Island.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Buffalo National River/Crooked Creek fishing report
reports.text:
Bass are good on cranks, Alabama rigs and swimbaits. Crappie are coming on like they should look on structure close to spawning flats and coves in 7-15 feet of water.
Crappie are good with the fish hanging around 10-15 feet depth of water; minnows and jigs are working, while anglers also are trolling crankbaits with success. Bass are hit-and-miss; they rate if fair, with crankbaits, jigs and jerkbaits getting the most responses.
